linkedin.text:
Most breaches don't start with genius hackers. They start with an ID changed in a URL.

When we test web applications, the findings that hurt most are rarely exotic. They are the ones automated scanners can't reason about:

→ Broken access control: one customer can read another customer's data
→ Sessions that never expire: one stolen cookie becomes full account access
→ Business logic gaps: coupons applied twice, prices edited in the request, checkout steps skipped
→ Injection in forgotten corners: old search boxes, filters and contact forms

A scanner gives you a score. A manual, OWASP-aligned test gives you reproducible findings, a clear fix for each one and a retest to prove it's closed.

When was the last time a human, not a tool, tried to break your app?

#Cybersecurity #PenetrationTesting #AppSec

Most AI support bots fail the same way: they answer questions they should never answer.

A refund policy invented on the spot. A legal claim. A price that doesn't exist. One confident wrong answer costs more than a hundred slow tickets.

So when we build an AI customer support agent, the refusal policy is designed and tested before launch, not added after the first incident:

→ Answers grounded only in your own knowledge base
→ Clear escalation rules that hand the conversation to a human at the right moment
→ A refusal policy tested against real edge cases
→ Analytics that show what customers ask and where the agent says no

The best support agent isn't the one that answers everything. It's the one that knows when not to.

How does your team decide what an AI agent is allowed to answer?

#AI #CustomerSupport #AIAgents
linkedin.first_comment: The question we ask every client first: which three answers would be most expensive if the agent got them wrong? Those become the first refusal tests. Details of how we build it: https://adyru.com/products

A payment integration that "works in testing" is not the same as one that survives real money.

The failures we see in production are almost never the happy path:

→ A customer clicks Pay twice and gets charged twice, because there's no idempotency key
→ A webhook arrives late, or twice, or forged, because nobody verifies signatures
→ Refunds handled by hand in a dashboard, with no record in your own system
→ Month-end reconciliation that takes a week because nothing matches

We integrate one payment rail end to end and harden it: tokenised capture, 3-D Secure, idempotency keys, signed webhooks, refunds and a reconciliation report from day one.

How long does your team spend reconciling payments every month?

#FinTech #Payments #Ecommerce
linkedin.first_comment: A simple test for any checkout: trigger the same payment request twice within a second. If you get two charges, idempotency is missing. Full scope of our Payment Gateway & Checkout Integration: https://adyru.com/products

linkedin.text:
In Web3, a bug isn't a ticket in the backlog. It's a transaction nobody can reverse.

That changes how a smart contract audit has to work:

→ Manual line-by-line review, because automated tools miss logic errors
→ Formal reasoning on the critical invariants: what must always be true, no matter what
→ Fuzzing to throw thousands of unexpected inputs at the contract before attackers do
→ A public-ready report your users can actually read, and verification that every fix landed

An audit isn't a badge for the website. It's the last chance to find the problem while it's still free to fix.

What's the one invariant your protocol can never break?

#Web3 #SmartContracts #BlockchainSecurity
linkedin.first_comment: If you're preparing for an audit, the best thing you can send on day one is a written list of invariants and the threat model you designed against. It makes the review faster and deeper. Our Smart Contract Security Audit: https://adyru.com/products

Every company has the same problem: the answer exists, but nobody can find it.

It's in a PDF from 2022, a shared drive folder, a policy someone updated last month. A RAG knowledge platform lets your team ask in plain language and get an answer with the source attached.

The difference between a demo and a system your team trusts is in the unglamorous parts:

→ Ingestion and chunking that keep tables and context intact
→ Hybrid retrieval, combining keyword and semantic search
→ Permissions, so people only see answers from documents they're allowed to read
→ Citations on every answer, so anyone can check the source in one click

If an AI answer can't show where it came from, it shouldn't be trusted.

Where does knowledge get lost in your company today?

#AI #RAG #KnowledgeManagement

→ Smooth frame rates on mid-range hardware, not just flagship devices
→ Analytics built in, so you see where players drop off

We build web and HTML5 games engineered for that reality: fast load, low memory, mid-range phones first.
